itemListElement.name: Cat Feeding Guide: Calories, Wet vs Dry, and Weight

blocks.headline: Cat Feeding Guide: Calories, Wet vs Dry, and Weight
blocks.description: How much to feed cats by life stage, why protein matters, and how to use a cat food calculator.

mainEntity.name: How many calories does an average indoor cat need per day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many spayed or neutered indoor cats need about 180 to 250 kcal daily, depending on weight and activity, but individual variation is wide. A 4 kg (9 lb) cat with low activity might target near 200 kcal; an active or underweight cat may need more. Use the cat food calculator as a starting point, then adjust by body condition.

mainEntity.name: Is wet food better than dry food for cats?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wet food adds moisture, which helps cats that drink little water and may support urinary health. Dry food is convenient and can support dental chewing in some cats. Many veterinarians suggest including wet food or ensuring ample water intake. Either can be complete if the label says it meets AAFCO standards for the cat’s life stage.

mainEntity.name: Why do vets say cats are obligate carnivores?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cats require nutrients found primarily in animal tissues, such as preformed vitamin A, arachidonic acid, and taurine. They are not designed to thrive on high-carbohydrate plant-based diets. Commercial cat foods are formulated to supply these nutrients; homemade diets need professional formulation.

mainEntity.name: How often should I feed my cat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most adult cats do well with two measured meals per day, or more small meals if you use automatic feeders. Free-feeding dry food contributes to obesity in many indoor cats. Kittens need three to four meals until about six months of age.

mainEntity.name: My cat is overweight. How much should I cut back?

acceptedAnswer.text: Aim for gradual loss: about 0.5 to 1 percent of body weight per week under veterinary supervision. That often means feeding 70 to 80 percent of maintenance calories, not half portions overnight. Weigh monthly and adjust; sudden crash dieting can cause hepatic lipidosis in cats.

mainEntity.name: Do senior cats need different food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Senior formulas often have adjusted protein and phosphorus for kidney health, but healthy older cats may stay on adult food. AAFP and AAHA feline life stage guidelines suggest focusing on muscle mass, hydration, and disease screening rather than age alone. Your vet may recommend a therapeutic diet if kidney or thyroid disease is present.
